subject: MAP: hosting handoff checklist and region escrow planning
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara@medispan.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: andrea.velez@medispan.com, tech-review@medispan.com
Date: 2028-07-21T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — hosting lanes and region expectations

Hi Lauren / Priyom,

Thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. The execs at MediSpan want a tight MAP that calls out:
- final hosting lane decision (hosted vs dedicated vs private) by Aug 10
- region fallback policy for EU patient data (primary eu-west, fallback: eu-central)
- evidence we can pass our security questionnaire by Aug 3 so procurement can start POs

We attached a first-pass MAP (sheet 1 = milestones). Can you confirm which Redwood contact will be the primary for the go/no-go signoff? Also very important: whether you can provide an escrow/fallback plan if eu-west has a sustained outage during initial 6-week rollout.

Appreciate a short runbook/ask list so we can align legal and infra.

Thanks,
Sara
Product Ops | MediSpan Technologies

Attachments: MAP_MediSpan_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2_evidence-overview.pdf (doc)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Sara Lee <sara@medispan.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — hosting lanes and region expectations

Sara — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front:
- Primary Redwood signoff owner: me (Lauren Bishop, Sr. Customer Success Manager) — I'll own the MAP and exec touchpoints.
- Security evidence: our SOC 2 summary + customer-facing controls can be provided by July 31; we can accelerate to Aug 1 if you need the PDF earlier.
- Escrow/fallback: we provide a region-fallback matrix and a temporary cross-region burst to Dedicated capacity for failover; details below.

Quick ask list for us to finalize the MAP:
1) Can you confirm the expected steady-state QPS and 99p latency target for the POC window? (we need this to size Dedicated vs Hosted)
2) Will PHI be processed in the POC or just de-identified data?
3) Who on your procurement/legal team will own the SOW and PO timeline?

Below is a short runbook that we'll add to the MAP file and publish to the shared Drive link:
- Week 0 (by Aug 1): Security evidence handover; provisioning request submitted to Redwood infra team.
- Week 1–2 (Aug 2–Aug 15): POC on Hosted (eu-west) with observability + token-level costing; smoke tests.
- Week 3 (Aug 16–Aug 23): If throughput/latency targets unmet or data isolation required -> switch to Dedicated trial (reserved pool in eu-central).
- Region fallback: Primary eu-west; automated traffic reroute to eu-central with warm Dedicated nodes and cache warmup policy. We will document RTO, RPO and manual rollback steps.

I'll loop Karthik on the exact sizing questions and Connor on the infra provisioning ETA.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0199

Lauren / Sara — adding sizing notes. Sara, quick bullet answers below based on the QPS / latency assumptions you asked about:

- If POC QPS <= 350 and 99p latency <= 700ms -> Hosted (eu-west) should reach targets with 1x standard pool and caching.
- If QPS > 350 or hard isolation required (PHI) -> Dedicated (eu-central) is recommended; reserve 2x cards to start (we can oversubscribe for burst).
- Private (on-prem/VPC) is feasible but extends close timeline by ~6–8 weeks for infra + compliance validation.

Sizing follow-ups we need from MediSpan by EOD Tue (July 25):
1) Estimated concurrent sessions during peak (15-min window)
2) Expected token length per call (avg and 95p)
3) Whether you require HSM-backed keying (if so, Private preferred)

Connor — can you confirm provisioning lead time for a eu-central dedicated pool if we need to spin up in week 3?

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, Sara Lee <sara@medispan.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — hosting lanes and region expectations

All — provisioning note for the MAP:

- Warm Dedicated pool in eu-central can be ready in 6 business days after commitment and signed MSA/PO. We have a fast-track path for POCs where we can reserve capacity in advance for a 2-week window; that carries a refundable commitment fee.
- Cross-region failover test (eu-west -> eu-central) will require a short blackout test during off hours; recommended runbook attached in Drive link.
- If MediSpan wants an escrow-style arrangement (independent compute reserve dedicated to your account) we need procurement sign-off and a refundable deposit to ensure capacity during major outages.

I'll add the exact provisioning timeline and cost delta to the MAP spreadsheet.

Connor O'Brien
Infra Ops | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Thanks team — this is excellent. Quick decisions from our side:
- We'll aim for Hosted (eu-west) during the POC (Aug 2–15) with the acceptance criteria you proposed. If we hit the latency Q99 target and token cost is within the threshold, we'll stay on Hosted.
- We will provision a contingency PO to enable a Dedicated trial in eu-central if required. Procurement requests the SOC2 evidence by Aug 1 and the pricing draft by July 29.
- PHI will not be processed in the POC (de-identified only) — we will revisit HSM needs during the Dedicated decision.

Next asks:
1) Lauren — can you send a single-row MAP summary (one-pager) we can share with procurement and our CTO?
2) Karthik/Connor — can you add the commitment fee number and the refundable deposit amount for the escrow option in the pricing draft?

We'll get the concurrent session and token length numbers to you by EOD July 26.

Best,
Andrea Velez
Head of Product Operations | MediSpan Technologies
